lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

The thirteenth publish is live since 01:46 UTC (6:46 PM MT Friday) at the same address. New on the page: fall's darker air and summer's see through swirl at the landing; the one smear for each flying petal and leaf is in the film's frames only. Checks before it, measured here: type check clean; the whole test run 1054 passed and 9 skipped; build exit 0 on engine 8192a3756180aae6; a second build without the sounds whose 17 files equal the security reviewer's list on 17 of 17 hashes; the first pictures' check passed; the review page rebuilt with 73 motion pictures. Stated: a fresh security reviewer of another model family answered no block and no warning; a helper read this build in a browser on its machine before the upload, nine loads live in 7 to 13 s, three real shakes that landed on the right season, 0 page messages, 33 buttons in every run. I looked at both of its sheets: every season whole, the swirl see through at 6 s after the landing, fall's storm under the darker air. After the upload, measured: the served index, build.json, the assets' table and the first pictures' table equal the local build, and unsigned requests answer 401 as Visibility Organization must. Not verified: a real graphics card, a phone, Safari, Firefox, the sound heard, the live address in a signed in browser.

Spring's glass after a shake is pushed by its builder, not on main and not on the live page yet. Stated by it: at the landing every one of the 26 runs has a head and a trail as at rest, the other seven guard pictures are equal, the shakes measure as on main, the whole test run 1061 passed and 8 skipped. By its own word below the bar still: on the pale storm of the landing the trails are pale on pale and the fine dew is mostly lost, and the trails stand as one bunch at the upper right. Its report and nine pictures came in at 6:47 PM MT; I read and look next, and it goes into chain 42 if it holds.

The petals' weave in the film (item 278) is not mended, said plainly. Its builder reports that both mends it proposed leave the fine ribs across the flying petals' smears as they were. Stated by it at 3840x2160 at the masters' tier: the strongest wave at film frame 1389 is 1.44 levels before and 1.43 with the mends, at frame 1388's rib 1.66 and 1.71, and about nine tenths of the weave is older than the one smear. I looked at its pictures at full size and at four times and see the same. Its new reading, not proven by a frame yet: the lens, because each sample of a frame sees a petal out of focus from one point of the lens, so the copies bunch as ribs. Decision 250: one last mend (a lens point of its own for each part of a sample, in the film's second mesh only, so the live page and the guard pictures cannot move) is being drawn at 3840 now, with floors set before any merge. If frame 1388 shows no gain it stops there and the weave stays open in the film: fine, two film frames long at a change with flown petals, below the bar at 4K.

The final render on his own computer. The first list of the Windows shader warnings is in (measured by the builder of the one file on a hosted Windows machine, Chrome 158 through Direct3D 11, one film frame: 25 program logs, all warnings, no error, on the functions decision 249 names). The Direct3D mender works on its three parts since 6:11 PM MT; its first part is due about 7:11 PM MT, the whole about 9:11 PM MT. Partner sent the Solar System build's finished render instructions for comparison; by that build's own word nothing in them has run on Windows, so the method is taken and not the proof. Eight points went to our builder to take where ours lacks them: stop when the page draws on another card than the one the system reports, read from the machine and not hard coded; the card's load read while frames draw; one verdict line and side by side pictures before his go; rules for Claude Code on long commands; keeping the machine awake; the unknowns with the check that settles each; the way back for the finished files; the sign in for the private repo on both machines. No final render is started in the cloud.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. Chain 42: spring's glass after a shake (pushed, being read), the patch for the stall at low quality if it comes whole, summer's fireflies and the seeds' dots, the frost line at film frame 668, the petals' weave if its last mend holds; then a critic for the change of season and a fourteenth publish. The Direct3D mend, merged like any part. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code; its builder's own guess for the last report is about 2:00 AM MT Saturday. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order (card loop, judged stills, record round, preview films, proof of the local render, cue sheet, README, last publish, gauntlet) and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks whiter and coarser than approved and its base darker; summer's pond at rest, flat pale plates where the approved has dark water (item 279); fall's storm paler than approved; spring's glass bare after a shake on the live page (mend pushed, pale on pale by its builder's own word); spring's fence and trails; the fireflies' flat bars at 4K (item 276); the seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277); the petals' weave at film frames 1388 and 1389 (item 278, two mends failed, a third being drawn); the frost line at film frame 668 (item 275); the stall at low quality on a software renderer; winter's four small items; fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272); the petals' fringe at film frame 680; the poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273, cause not found, it passed on a second run again).
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger at 01:41 UTC: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.
